questions: Should the function traverse subdirectories recursively when searching for matching files, or only examine files directly in the source directory?
If a file with the same name already exists in the target directory, should it be overwritten, skipped, or raise an error?
Should the function preserve the directory structure of matched files from subdirectories when moving them to the target directory?
Should symlinks be followed when searching for files, and if moved, should the symlink or the target file be moved?
Should the function move hidden files (starting with '.') if they match the pattern?
If moving a file fails (e.g., permission error), should the function continue with remaining files or stop immediately?
Should the pattern matching be case-sensitive? The default pattern uses [A-Za-z] but re.match behavior depends on flags.
Should the function create intermediate directories in the target path if they don't exist, or only create the target directory itself?
